tagline: Foundational certification in the AMS AI Operator Licence Program

## Appendix A — Tier 1 Assessment Design

The Tier 1 assessment is the 80% gate for certification. It is a 20-question multiple-choice test drawn randomly from a bank of 60 questions. The question bank is maintained as a separate companion document (Tier 1 Quiz Bank, XLSX) to allow direct LMS import.

#### Assessment parameters

| Format | 20 multiple-choice questions, randomized per attempt from a 60-question bank |
| --- | --- |
| Pass rate | 80% (16 out of 20) |
| Attempts | 3, with question randomization between attempts |
| Time limit | 30 minutes |
| Annual renewal | 15-question refresher, 30–60 minute module covering updates since previous certification |

#### Question distribution across modules

| Module | Questions per 20-question attempt | Bank allocation | Coverage emphasis |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1.1 — What Is AI? | 4 | 12 | Definitions, categories, AI vs. traditional software, what AI is not |
| 1.2 — AI at AMS | 3 | 8 | Approved register, tier model, governance structure, your role |
| 1.3 — AI Risks | 5 | 14 | Hallucinations, bias, errors, confidence problem |
| 1.4 — Privacy & Data | 5 | 14 | Saskatchewan privacy law, classification, approved vs. unapproved, Shadow AI |
| 1.5 — Reporting | 3 | 12 | Human-bookend model, incident categories, ServiceNow process, escalation |

## Appendix B — Data Classification Quick Reference

Intended as a one-page desk reference. Print-ready version in the companion design pack.

| Classification | Examples | Approved AI tools | External AI tools |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Public | Published press releases, public financial reports, job postings, 3shealth.ca content | Permitted | Permitted only in reputable tools — but prefer approved tools |
| Internal | Internal process docs, non-personal meeting notes, drafts, aggregate analytics | Permitted in approved tenanted tools | Prohibited |
| Confidential / PHI / PII | Employee records, payroll, benefit claims, EFAP data, HR investigations, anything tied to a named person | Permitted only where tool is approved for this classification; PHI requires de-identification unless documented consent | Prohibited |
| Restricted | Credentials, legal hold material, privileged communications, critical source code | Prohibited pending Steering Committee review for agentic/local scenarios | Prohibited |

## Appendix C — Glossary

| Agent (AI agent) | An AI system that can take action beyond producing content — calling APIs, updating records, initiating workflows. Higher risk profile than a generative assistant. |
| --- | --- |
| AIGC | AI Governance Committee — the overarching governance body for AI use across Saskatchewan's health system. The AI Policy that sits above the AUP is maintained by AIGC. |
| AI Steering Committee | The operational body that reviews proposed AI tools, evaluates risk, and decides what gets added to the Approved AI Tool Register. |
| AMS | Application Management Services — the 3sHealth team responsible for administrative application platforms (Oracle Fusion, ServiceNow, M365, BI). |
| Approved tool | An AI tool that appears on the AMS Approved AI Tool Register, for the specific data classification in use, and at the Tier level held by the user. |
| AUP | AI Acceptable Use Policy — the 3sHealth policy that defines how AI may be used. Child policy under the broader AI Policy maintained by AIGC. |
| Bias | Systematic skew in AI output reflecting skew in training data. Distinct from hallucination. |
| FACTS | Tier 2 framework for evaluating AI output: Factual accuracy, Attribution, Completeness, Tone, Safety. |
| FOIP / LA FOIP | Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act and Local Authority Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act (Saskatchewan). |
| Generative AI | AI systems that produce new content — text, code, images — rather than classifying or predicting. The primary focus of this program. |
| Hallucination | AI-generated content that is confidently presented and factually wrong. The most important failure mode to internalize. |
| HIPA | Health Information Protection Act (Saskatchewan). Governs personal health information. Enforced by the Saskatchewan Information and Privacy Commissioner. |
| Human-bookend model | The accountability structure for AI-assisted work: human at the start to define and prompt, AI in the middle to execute, human at the end to verify and take accountability. |
| Machine learning | AI that learns a model from historical data and applies it to new inputs. Usually narrower than generative AI. |
| PHI | Personal Health Information. Governed by HIPA. |
| PIPEDA | Personal Information Protection and Electronic Documents Act (Federal). Applies to commercial activities. |
| PII | Personal Information — data that identifies an individual. |
| Prompt | The input to a generative AI tool. The content you type or paste that tells the AI what to do. |
| Shadow AI | Use of AI tools not on the approved register for 3sHealth work. A policy violation in itself, per AUP Section 12. |
| Tenant | The slice of a cloud service that belongs to a specific organization. Tenanted M365 Copilot operates inside the 3sHealth tenant boundary; personal Copilot does not. |
